bestPractices.title: AVIF Compression Best Practices
bestPractices.description: Follow these expert tips to get the best results from AVIF compression.

tips.title: Leverage Next-Gen Compression
tips.content: AVIF offers 30-50% better compression than WebP and 50-70% better than JPEG. Use quality 75-85 for web images—AVIF maintains excellent quality at lower settings due to advanced perceptual optimization. For high-end photography or HDR content, use quality 85-95 to fully utilize AVIF's 10-bit and 12-bit color depth capabilities.

tips.title: Optimize for Modern Browsers
tips.content: AVIF is supported by 90%+ of users (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari 16+). Use <picture> element with AVIF primary, WebP fallback, and JPEG/PNG for maximum compatibility. AVIF encoding is slower than JPEG/WebP, so pre-generate images during build time rather than on-the-fly for production websites.

tips.title: Maximize Quality-to-Size Ratio
tips.content: AVIF excels at high-quality images at small file sizes. Use it for hero images, product photography, and high-resolution displays where quality matters. Enable adaptive quantization and film grain synthesis for photographic content. For simple graphics or animations, WebP or PNG may be more efficient despite larger file sizes.

tips.title: Strategic Implementation
tips.content: Start with high-impact images (hero sections, product photos, featured content). Monitor encoding time and server load—AVIF encoding can be 5-10x slower than JPEG. Use faster encoding speeds (6-8) for development and slower speeds (2-4) for production to balance quality and processing time. Consider CDN support for AVIF delivery.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Common questions about AVIF compression and our AVIF compressor tool.

items.question: What is AVIF format?
items.answer: AVIF is a next-generation image format based on the AV1 video codec, offering superior compression efficiency and advanced features like HDR support and wide color gamut.

items.question: How does AVIF compare to JPEG and WebP?
items.answer: AVIF typically provides 50% better compression than JPEG and 20-30% better than WebP while maintaining exceptional image quality.

items.question: Do all browsers support AVIF?
items.answer: Modern browsers like Chrome, Firefox, and Safari support AVIF, but older browsers may not. It's recommended to provide fallback formats.

items.question: Does AVIF support transparency?
items.answer: Yes, AVIF fully supports transparency with alpha channel, similar to PNG and WebP.

items.question: What is HDR support in AVIF?
items.answer: AVIF supports High Dynamic Range (HDR) imaging with 10-bit and 12-bit color depths, enabling stunning image quality for compatible displays.

items.question: When should I use AVIF?
items.answer: AVIF is best for modern web applications, mobile apps, and scenarios where maximum compression efficiency and quality are priorities.
